Well, see... the thing is that you're going to lose some muscle mass if you're not also exercising. Not all of the weight you lose will be in fat. The thing about muscles is they increase your bmr more than the equivalent mass of fat, so you'll want to hang onto them as much as possible just to make it that much easier on yourself in the long run. And the thing about your heart is that it's a muscle too. So you're weakening it along with your other muscles. That's not good.

I think that's one of the reasons why cardio is important when you're losing weight. The other reason is that cardio is also fantastic for fat burning, especially if done in the morning after you wake up before you have breakfast. When you wake up before breakfast, your body has a lot less fuel to work with, so it more readily goes after your fat stores. Otherwise, cardio usually has to go on longer than 30 minutes to really start burning fat.

I'd also recommend some form of resistance training.

So basically, I think you should probably eat a bit more just to account for the exercise you're doing. If you don't, you're probably going to feel like total shit, and I'm not a doctor but I think it might even be bad for your immune system.
